question: Does the linked-class sum rule predict the cheapest growth's dimension on every census arrangement with a birth (fitting) and on six-knot samples (test)?

definitions.linked: two classes of one round whose partners share a neighbour
definitions.rule: largest sum of class sizes over linked components

public_inputs.reused: TOUCH-CENSUS-20261118-001B arrlib.py; its run's per-arrangement results (runs/touch-census) select the census part

forbidden_inputs: Changing the rule or predictions after reading the six-knot results

predictions.P1: six knots: dimension = linked sum, no false positive
predictions.P2: sum on larger components; a path of three gives 2

stop_rule: One run; read-out; referee hand-off; report.

amendments.change: merge.py printed a dictionary with tuple keys; keys converted to text. No case, rule, prediction or number changed.
